from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Histograms show discrete data grouped in intervals.",
            "Narrowing intervals smooths the chart significantly.",
            "As data points grow, bars form a curve.",
            "This curve is the Probability Density Function.",
            "It describes probability density for continuous variables."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Intuitive Hook: From Discrete to Continuous", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define objects
        # Histogram bars (representing discrete data)
        bars = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=0.8, height=np.random.rand()*2+0.5, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.5) for _ in range(6)])
        bars.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1, aligned_edge=DOWN)
        self.place_in_area(bars, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.6)

        # Curve (the PDF)
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 6, 1], y_range=[0, 3, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 2 * np.exp(-(x - 3)**2), x_range=[0, 6], color="#FF7F50")
        curve_area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0, 6], color="#87CEFA", opacity=0.3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(bars))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GRAY), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        # Morph bars (simulated)
        self.play(FadeOut(bars), FadeIn(curve))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GRAY), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.play(FadeIn(curve_area))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GRAY), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF7F50"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(GRAY), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#87CEFA"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Core Mathematical Properties", [
            "PDFs have two main mathematical properties.",
            "First, the function must be non-negative.",
            "Second, the total area must equal one.",
            "This represents total probability certainty.",
            "Total area under the curve is always one."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display the probability mass function formula.
        pdf_text = MathTex(r"f(x) \geq 0").set_color(WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(pdf_text, 'B2', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Write(pdf_text))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight non-negative constraint
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF7F50"))
        # Already have f(x) >= 0 on screen
        self.play(Indicate(pdf_text))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show the constraint that total area equals one.
        integral_text = MathTex(r"\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x) \, dx = 1").set_color("#32CD32")
        self.place_at_grid(integral_text, 'D3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#32CD32"))
        self.play(Write(integral_text))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 & 5 ===
        # Shaded area under curve animation
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 10, 2], y_range=[0, 0.5, 0.1], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.1 * (1 - x/10), x_range=[0, 10])
        area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0, 10], color=BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        
        graph_group = VGroup(axes, curve, area)
        self.place_in_area(graph_group, 'E1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve), FadeIn(area))
        
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#32CD32"))
        self.play(area.animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Continuous variables have zero point probability.",
            "We measure probability over an interval instead.",
            "Area under the curve equals the probability.",
            "Integral calculates this area between two points.",
            "Visualize probability as a shaded curve slice."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Interpreting Probability as Area", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup Axes and Curve
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3, 1], y_range=[0, 1.5, 0.5], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: np.exp(-x**2), x_range=[-3, 3], color=WHITE)
        plot_group = VGroup(axes, curve)
        self.place_in_area(plot_group, 'A1', 'E6', scale_factor=0.6)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(plot_group))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF7F50")
        interval_start = -1
        interval_end = 0.5
        line_start = axes.c2p(interval_start, 0)
        line_end = axes.c2p(interval_start, axes.c2p(0, np.exp(-interval_start**2))[1])
        # placeholder for visual interval logic
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#87CEFA")
        area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[interval_start, interval_end], color="#87CEFA", opacity=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(area))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FF69B4")
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "PDF defines probability density, not probability itself.",
            "The peak indicates the most likely value.",
            "Changing parameters alters the distribution shape."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Conceptual Check", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define objects
        # Normal distribution curve
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-4, 4], y_range=[0, 1], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.5)
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: np.exp(-x**2/2) / np.sqrt(2*np.pi), color=WHITE)
        area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[-4, 4], color=BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.place_in_area(VGroup(axes, curve, area), "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve), FadeIn(area))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF7F50"))
        dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        dot.move_to(axes.c2p(0, 1/np.sqrt(2*np.pi)))
        peak_label = Text("Peak", font_size=20, color=YELLOW).next_to(dot, UP)
        self.play(FadeIn(dot), Write(peak_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#32CD32"))
        
        # Shift parameter animation
        new_curve = axes.plot(lambda x: np.exp(-(x-1)**2/2) / np.sqrt(2*np.pi), color=WHITE)
        new_area = axes.get_area(new_curve, x_range=[-4, 4], color=BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(curve, new_curve),
            Transform(area, new_area),
            dot.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(1, 1/np.sqrt(2*np.pi))),
            peak_label.animate.next_to(axes.c2p(1, 1/np.sqrt(2*np.pi)), UP)
        )
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: From Discrete to Continuous
sections.content: Briefly review histograms of discrete data (e.g., shoe sizes). Transition to the limit: as the number of data points increases and intervals narrow, the bar chart smooths into a continuous curve. Define the PDF as the 'shape' of probability for continuous variables.
sections.example: Visualizing a crowd of rabbits: instead of counting individual weights, we see a smooth curve representing the density of weights across the population.

sections.title: Defining the Core Mathematical Properties
sections.content: Introduce the two mandatory conditions for a valid PDF: 1) Non-negativity (f(x) ≥ 0) and 2) Normalization (the total area under the curve must equal 1). Use a shaded area animation under a curve to represent total probability.
sections.example: A 'Robot Battery Life' curve: The area under the curve between 0 and 10 hours equals 1 (representing 100% certainty that the battery eventually dies).

sections.title: Interpreting Probability as Area
sections.content: Explain that for continuous variables, the probability of an exact value is zero. Instead, we calculate probability over an interval. P(a < X < b) is the integral of the PDF from a to b. Emphasize that visual 'area' = 'probability'.
sections.example: Calculating the probability that a delivery drone arrives between 14:00 and 14:15 by highlighting the specific shaded vertical slice of the time-density curve.

sections.title: Summary and Conceptual Check
sections.content: Recap: PDF is not probability itself, but the 'density' of probability. Reiterate that the peak indicates where the variable is most likely to be found. Final visual: A shifting curve showing how changing parameters changes the distribution shape.
sections.example: A 'Growth Hormone' experiment: show how the curve shifts right as the average weight of experimental mice increases, keeping the total area fixed at 1.
